flat-once.design_notes:
The branch is the three prior-spike commits (15c72a8, 15bce74, bc0e0b8) cherry-picked and squashed into one commit on a17747d. I restored everything outside the design: crates/gossip-bench, the figures, deploy/, and the root, nginx and server READMEs and CRDT.md (these held prior-spike benchmark prose and regenerated figures that no longer match). I added a "Design notes" section to crates/gabion/README.md that says it is authoritative for this branch where the older sections describe main's resend-until-acked loop.

Mechanism, as implemented:
- Round: send the changes since the last round, newest first, to ceil(ln n + 3) distinct picks. Picks are a partial Fisher-Yates shuffle, so sampling is without replacement.
- Fanout depends only on n. c=3 is the existing defaults::GOSSIP_COVERAGE_MARGIN.
- Forward once: both dirty rings are cleared at the end of every round via end_round, so each merged change is forwarded at most once.
- Repair: a heartbeat's first pick also carries 256 cells of the rotating repair slice. Threshold rounds carry none. A cut slice resumes via resume_repair_at.
- The peer frontier is a skip hint only: the dirty lanes consult it, the repair lane never does, and last_sent was removed.
- The shared scheduler (500 ms heartbeat, threshold rounds, 5 ms floor) is unchanged. Main's per-rule accounting is not fixed.

Adaptations, all documented in the README:
1. GOSSIP_SEND_QUEUE_CAPACITY 128 -> 512. A round now queues every pick's whole frame at once. The send pool slot index widened from u8 to usize, because a pool above 255 slots wrapped to an empty free list. Each pick gets an even share of the free slots, and a frame over its share loses its tail (repair first, then the oldest changes) with a power-of-two warning.
2. A round that cannot give every pick a slot (blocked socket) is deferred whole, so its changes are kept and the emit floor restarts.
3. The repair slice size is the const defaults::GOSSIP_REPAIR_CELLS_PER_ROUND, not a GossipConfig field. I tried a field first, but gossip-bench's legacy scenarios.rs builds GossipConfig as a literal and cannot be edited (rule 4). This departs from the rule that parameters are config fields. Config fields the harness sets (fanout, max_cells_per_tick, send_queue_capacity, etc.) remain and still work. fanout is now only the floor under the coverage pick, and max_cells_per_tick caps each pick's frame.
4. Frame filling collapsed visit_local_dirty, visit_forwarded_dirty and the separate peer and non-peer fill functions into one CellStore::fill_gossip_frame(max_cells, repair_cells, peer, out). I added Packets::abandon, removed PeerFrontierTable last_sent and lacks_indices, and made DirtyRing::clear keep overflow_seq so overflow warnings stay power-of-two spaced. The warning texts name the new cause.
5. The wasm engine's doc comments and sizing note, the nginx directive help strings and the crdt bench were adapted. admin.rs doc comments were updated.

direct-ack.design_notes:
The design is unchanged: delta-state anti-entropy on a full mesh (Almeida et al., arXiv 1603.01529 and 1803.02750), with per-peer cumulative acks. This commit fixes the audited issues.

**Major fix: peers starved when the send pool ran dry.**
- The round rotation now advances by the number of peers actually visited (`next_round_start = start + visited`), not by one. Peers the pool could not reach go first in the next round.
- The send pool now sizes itself to the live peer count. It holds `max(gossip.send_queue_capacity, GOSSIP_SEND_SLOTS_PER_PEER × peers)` slots. `GOSSIP_SEND_SLOTS_PER_PEER = 2` is a new constant in `gabion::defaults`. A round can therefore queue at least one packet for every peer, and a second round's worth of slots remains free while the first drains.
- The pool grows on bootstrap and on `PeerEvent::Added` only, never per packet. It does not shrink when peers leave. The growth reserves `send_pool`, `send_free` and `send_pending` up front, so steady state does not allocate.
- Slot indices are now `SendSlot = u32`. The old `u8` capped the pool at 255, below prod-4x's 299 peers, and wrapped to an empty free list above 255.
- This is a documented adaptation in the README Design notes, section "The send pool is sized to the peer count". The papers assume an unbounded channel. `send_queue_capacity` is now a minimum.
- The wasm `engine.rs` comment that described the 255 ceiling is rewritten.

**Minor fixes:**
- **Retransmission floor.** It is now `config.tick_interval` (`rto_floor_ms`, computed once at construction), as spec section 3.4 says: `max(2·RTT, 1 tick)`. `GOSSIP_MIN_RTO_MILLIS` is removed and the README is updated. Behaviour is identical at the 500 ms heartbeat and differs only in tests that use a 100 ms tick.
- **`server/identity.rs` doc.** The same-incarnation restart note now states the full window. A peer's old ack covers every new sequence up to the old boot's high-water mark, and a packet lost anywhere in that range is not retransmitted until sequences pass it. I did not add detection; the audit offered rewording as an option.
- **Stale README.** I deleted the "What we measured" subsections for steady-state convergence, scale, resilience and coverage-fanout, plus the six `figures/*.svg` they referenced, because they described a design that no longer exists. I kept the error-budget, min-emit-clamp and heartbeat-threshold figures, which cover the unchanged threshold machinery. They carry an honest caveat that they predate direct mail. I removed the stale "peer frontier" and "coverage-fanout pick" phrasing from the References section.
- **nginx README.** The `send_queue_capacity` description now says "minimum; grows to two slots per live peer".

**Still true from the earlier result:**
- Config fields that are accepted but ignored: `fanout`, `rng_seed`, `forwarded_dirty_capacity`, `peer_capacity`.
- `CRDT.md` is bannered as out of date, not rewritten.
- Main's shared scheduler and its per-rule threshold accounting are untouched.
- The `crates/gossip-bench` tree hash is unchanged.

plumtree.design_notes:
Documented in crates/gabion/README.md under "Design notes: Plumtree dissemination" (mechanism, parameters, adaptations, invariant-to-code table).

What it does. Plumtree kept per root (Leitao et al. SRDS 2007 for the protocol, HyParView DSN 2007 for views, riak_core_broadcast for per-root sets). A message is (origin, incarnation, origin sequence). The active view is ceil(ln n + 3) random peers, kept as a uniform reservoir sample over PeerEvent::Added and refilled on Removed. Eager and lazy are a per-root bitmask over view positions, so they partition the view. Eager frames carry full cells. A duplicate eager delivery sends PRUNE. A lazy IHAVE digest goes to lazy_targets=2 lazy peers per heartbeat (full digest every 8). An IHAVE above the receiver's watermark starts a 500 ms timer, and GRAFT is sent only when it expires. Relayed changes go out in a relay round relay_floor_ms (5) after arrival. Local changes go out in main's unchanged heartbeat and threshold rounds, and rule_pending accounting is untouched.

Faithfulness invariants. PRUNE: only handle_data on FrameKind::Eager rows that did not raise a cell. GRAFT: only check_timers on Missing records, which only on_ihave creates. Per-root partition: roots[slot].lazy mask with eager = occupied & !lazy. Origin sequence kept: CellStore::merge_remote_row. Hybrid: extra_random is a PlumtreeConfig field defaulting to 0, sends FrameKind::Random frames, and is counted as data. Shared tree: not used. I-1..I-6: all communication is GossipTransport datagrams. The only globals are none. Membership comes only from PeerEvent. Per-node state is pre-sized. All randomness comes from the node's SplitMix64. There is no HashMap iteration (sorted scratch vectors only).

Adaptations (each documented with reason):
(1) Cells are state: one entry per cell per round, newest state; a duplicate means the merge did not raise the count.
(2) IHAVE carries a per-origin watermark, because superseded sequences cannot be told apart from losses; holes below the watermark are closed by NACK and the repair slice.
(3) UDP: per-edge packet numbers in min_origin_sequence, a 64-packet receive window, NACK as (window start, missing bitmask) after one relay-floor grace and every nack_retry_ms (100), at most 10 tries, answered from a 512-packet resend ring under the original number (FrameKind::Resent).
(4) Off-tree arrivals (repair, pull, random) are kept unforwarded; the tree's first delivery of them is forwarded and does not prune. Without this the repair slice winning a race made nodes prune their own parent. This took prod-typical from 2% never-converged to 0.
(5) first_contact_pull=true: the first sight of an unknown origin sends PULL, which is separate from GRAFT so GRAFT keeps its invariant.
(6) The repair slice of main is retained, narrowed to 256 cells per heartbeat to one random peer, as the convergence backstop.
(7) The relay round and protocol timers are armed as fresh clock tickers (Clock::ticker, first tick consumed), so no tokio::time is used.
(8) Directed views, with no NEIGHBOR handshake, because membership is full.
(9) GRAFT asks from the watermark held when the announcement arrived.

Wire and API changes. The solution contract is unchanged and compiles, and the gossip-bench tree is byte-identical (hash verified after commit). New: wire::FrameKind in 3 flag bits, wire/control.rs (IHave, Graft, Prune, Nack, Pull; 72-byte header plus 28-byte entries, HMAC-covered when auth is on), Packets::next_into_numbered and abandon, Observation.origin_sequence, CellStore::{origin_watermark, merge_remote_row}, PlumtreeConfig plus GossipRuntime::with_plumtree. GossipConfig is untouched because gossip-bench's legacy scenarios.rs builds it by struct literal, so the parameters live in PlumtreeConfig, whose Default reads gabion::defaults::PLUMTREE_*.

No-op or changed fields. GossipConfig::fanout is a no-op (documented). CellStoreConfig dirty-ring capacities are kept for the contract, but the rings are cleared after each event and no longer read by the runtime. AdminSnapshot.local/forwarded_dirty_len now report the changes queued for the next round, and last/peak_effective_fanout report the peers a round pushed to. dirty_ticks counts rounds that pushed changes.

snow.design_notes:
Documented in 'Design notes' in crates/gabion/README.md (updated). Changes in this round:
(1) MAJOR ring cycle/wrap bug: ranges are now clockwise intervals [lo, hi) of the sorted ring, located by position in the receiver's own view (len = (pos(hi) - pos(lo)) mod m), not offsets into a view-size-dependent rotation. hi is always carried (Child.hi and Ctrl::Data.hi are no longer Option). The root's own interval is everyone but itself with hi = root, and the root sits at the midpoint of the nodes it covers exactly as before. Because root is now only ever the hi of the outermost ranges, Ring::children no longer takes a root argument (the child function is still a pure function of local view and carried range; the root travels as hi). Missing lo/hi are still inserted into a scratch copy only. A node with a non-empty range always gets children, so it cannot ack as a leaf with unserved nodes. Wire layout: the 'hi?' None marker is gone; CTRL_MAX_LEN unchanged (62).
(2) MAJOR payload budget: begin_broadcast encodes root packets against max_payload_bytes minus (wire::EXT_PREFIX_LEN, now pub, + CTRL_MAX_LEN), so reframing at the root and at every relay fits. Tree sends that fail to queue (no free buffer, or frame over budget) are now counted (send_dropped_total) and logged with the power-of-two rate-limited warn in the three-question style, naming send_queue_capacity and max_payload_bytes.
(3) MAJOR repair lane: GOSSIP_REPAIR_CELLS_PER_TICK 64 -> 256, the heartbeat repair slice of the study's flat-once design (research.md 3.4), still one random peer per heartbeat. Documented in defaults.rs and README as the paper not defining a repair lane, with the source. I did not adopt main's lane (fill-to-frame to ceil(ln n + 3) peers) because that would be a second push path next to the tree.
(4) Minor: Relay now stores the forwarded children (addr plus carried range) in an arrayvec::ArrayVec and matches acks and repeats against that frozen set. This needed MAX_CHILDREN 16 -> 8 (k clamped 2..=8, u8 ack masks), GOSSIP_TREE_RELAY_CAPACITY 2048 -> 1024 to bound memory (~1 KB per relay), and gabion gained the arrayvec workspace dependency. serious.problem: Parents and backbone views are picked at random among the peers known *so far*, and the structure is rebuilt after each Added event. Discovery delivers members one event at a time in a fixed order. In the harness that is pod-index order, and k8s EndpointSlices are also ordered. So when the first class-t peer arrives it is the only candidate, and every node attaches to the same parent in each tree. Each tree becomes a star: one hub with every non-class node as its leaf child. The backbone view also always holds the first ~5 class-mates. Thicket's defining property, balanced forwarding with bounded interior degree, is lost, and leaf_child has no cap (repair.rs:341-343). The design notes claim a 'backbone view of random class-mates' and a random parent, which is false in practice. Effects on results: changes travel leaf, hub, all leaves in 2 hops, which flatters latency. The hub's send queue runs near capacity (depth 186 at 80 pods; 427-461 of 512 at 183 pods in loss-5, loss-burst and hot-key), so prod-peak and prod-4x (about 200 leaves per hub) are likely to cut frames. A hub crash removes a whole tree for 10-12 s.

thicket.design_notes:
Updated "Design notes: Thicket dissemination" in crates/gabion/README.md. Changes against the audit:

MAJOR (lazy repair blind to holes): IHAVE now names each cell version, so a message lost below a later one from the same origin is still announced. An entry is origin node_id, incarnation, sequence, plus rule fingerprint, key hash and bucket (64 B, wire/control.rs; only Ihave and Graft use the wide entry, other kinds keep 28 B). The receiver does find_cell and starts Plumtree's missing timer (500 ms) only if it holds neither that version nor a newer one. A GRAFT names the same entries and is answered with the current cell of each; a GRAFT that went unanswered is sent again, up to 3 times (THICKET_GRAFT_ATTEMPTS). Tree repair is unchanged: the backbone GRAFT is sent only for changes whose tree is the node's own class. Per-cell queue: changes made locally or delivered by a tree edge (Arrival Local or Eager) are queued once per cell version (generation-stamped, bounded by cell capacity) and announced at the next heartbeat to THICKET_LAZY_TARGETS=2 random peers, a cell that changed again being named once at its newest version. Cells delivered by GRAFT or repair slice are not announced. The origin high-water digest, `announced`, `want`, `full_digest_due`, THICKET_IHAVE_FULL_EVERY, `highest_origin_sequence` and `visit_cells_after` are deleted.

Because an IHAVE is sent once, to 2 peers, a change older than its announcement (partition heal, long outage) is only recovered by the existing repair slice (256 cells per heartbeat to one random peer). That remains the documented non-Thicket backstop; I did not tune it, so az-partition and loss-burst keep a large never-converged tail.

Joiner catch-up (audit minor 3): since members no longer send a digest, a node whose store is empty when discovery adds a peer sends a new Pull control frame (kind 6, no entries); the peer answers with its next repair slice, and while a slice teaches the joiner something it asks the same peer for the next, so the transfer is paced by the round trip instead of one 4096-cell burst. A request unanswered for a heartbeat (for example the peer has not discovered the joiner yet, so it ignores the frame) goes to another random peer, up to THICKET_CATCH_UP_ATTEMPTS=6. A debug run showed a joiner now holds the full cell set about 0.55 s after its first request.

Minor PRUNE (fixed): PRUNE is sent on every duplicate eager packet as in Plumtree; the per-sender throttle and `last_prune_ms` are removed, and THICKET_NACK_RETRY_MS now documents only the NACK wait.

Minor PROBE (fixed): `probed_seq` replaced by `probes_left`, reset to THICKET_PROBE_REPEATS=3 by each eager packet, so a lost probe is repeated at the next heartbeats and a lost tail still shows.

Minor wildcard-bind self class (not fixed): still hashes transport.local_addr() and is documented as such; it needs the header node id and is out of scope for the sim comparison.

New defaults (documented in gabion::defaults and the README parameter table): THICKET_MISSING_CAPACITY=4096, THICKET_GRAFT_ATTEMPTS=3, THICKET_PROBE_REPEATS=3, THICKET_CATCH_UP_ATTEMPTS=6; THICKET_REPAIR_CELLS (256) now also paces catch-up requests. Still constants and not GossipConfig fields, because gossip-bench/src/scenarios.rs builds GossipConfig as a full struct literal. Docs also corrected: the wire header table now shows 80 bytes with edge_sequence, and CRDT.md no longer mentions highest_origin_sequence. Rule 5 untouched: the 500 ms heartbeat and threshold scheduler are as on main, and per-rule threshold accounting is not changed.

gossipsub.design_notes:
The design notes are in `crates/gabion/README.md` under "Design notes: GossipSub mesh dissemination".

Mechanism
- One topic. A message is one gossip datagram of cells, named by a 64-bit XXH3 hash of its bytes. A libp2p deployment may choose its message-id function, and Eth2 uses a content hash.
- Each shared-scheduler round (500 ms tick plus threshold rounds, unchanged) publishes the local dirty-ring cells above a published-sequence watermark to the node's mesh peers.
- A datagram seen for the first time is merged, cached, and forwarded verbatim to mesh peers. The sender and the publisher are excluded.
- A 1 s mesh heartbeat runs GRAFT up to D when the mesh is below D_lo, and PRUNE down to D when it is above D_hi. It then sends IHAVE (ids only) from the newest 3 of 5 cache heartbeats to max(D_lazy, 0.25 x non-mesh) random non-mesh peers.
- IWANT is sent immediately (iwant_delay_ms = 0, so there is no field for it). The advertiser serves it from the bounded mcache.
- A GRAFT is refused with PRUNE when the sender is unknown, in backoff, or the mesh is at D_hi.
- Parameters are the spec defaults and live in `gabion::defaults::GOSSIPSUB_*`.

Faithfulness
- Full payloads go only to mesh peers or in answer to IWANT.
- IHAVE carries ids only.
- Mesh size is kept in [D_lo, D_hi] only by heartbeat maintenance and the D_hi check on GRAFT.
- Messages are served only from the mcache, which is bounded by heartbeat age and by capacity.
- Randomness comes only from the node's seeded SplitMix64. Nodes communicate only through GossipTransport datagrams, there are no globals, and membership comes only from PeerEvents.
- The seen cache, mcache, send pool and peer scratch lists are sized at construction.

Deviations from the spec, all documented in the README
1. UDP instead of libp2p streams. Each control message is its own HMAC-covered datagram, and IHAVE/IWANT lists are split to fit the payload limit. Control messages are not retransmitted.
2. Flood publishing is off (the v1.1 default is on) because it would break "full payloads only to mesh peers or on IWANT".
3. Omitted because the cluster is trusted or because they conflict with I-2: peer scoring and all thresholds, D_score, D_out, opportunistic grafting, the IWANT retransmission limit, IHAVE flood limits, and peer exchange on PRUNE (membership comes only from discovery). Pruning keeps a random D mesh peers.
4. The mesh heartbeat rides the shared tick instead of using a second ticker. It fires on the first tick after 1 s has elapsed, and on the first tick of a node's life, before that tick's publish. This keeps the wasm `ManualClock`, which supports only one ticker, working. With the 500 ms tick this is exactly every 2nd tick.
5. Bounds that the spec leaves open: the mcache holds 4,096 messages of 1,400 B, and the seen cache holds 32,768 ids. Eviction is FIFO.
6. No repair lane, no frontier acks and no anti-entropy. This is the design, not a shortcut, and its consequences are real. A datagram lost on a cluster with at most D peers (full mesh, so no IHAVE targets) is recovered only by the next message touching the same cell. A joiner never receives settled cells from earlier buckets.

Code shape
- New `SendQueue` (`gossip/send_queue.rs`): a refcounted pool in which one buffer is queued to many destinations. It replaces the runtime's `send_pool`, `send_pending` and `send_free`.
- New `gossip/pubsub.rs` holds `PubSubConfig`, `IdRing` and `MessageCache`. New `gossip/runtime/pubsub.rs` holds the mesh, publish and control handlers. New `wire/control.rs` holds the control codec (`FLAG_CONTROL`).
- Small additions: `PacketBuf::set_bytes`, `wire::is_control`, `observation_from_wire` made `pub(crate)`, `CellStore::clear_forwarded_dirty`. The last is called after each merge because datagrams are forwarded verbatim. This stops a spurious "Forwarded dirty ring overflowed ... convergence will depend on repair scans" warning in large runs.
- `PubSubConfig` is set with `GossipRuntime::with_pubsub(cfg)` and is deliberately not a field of `GossipConfig`. A new field would break the literal in the legacy gossip-bench scenarios, which cannot be edited, and would force edits in the server, nginx and wasm adapters.
- Public API changes: `PeerEntry.peer_slot` is replaced by `in_mesh: bool`. `AdminSnapshot::last_effective_fanout` and `peak_effective_fanout` now report the mesh degree used by the last publish round.

No-ops
- `GossipConfig::fanout` and `defaults::GOSSIP_FANOUT`/`GOSSIP_COVERAGE_MARGIN` are unused. The `gossip.fanout` env var and config key still parse.
- `CellStoreConfig.peer_capacity` and `forwarded_dirty_capacity` and the peer-frontier table are left allocated but unused by the runtime. `fill_gossip_frame*` stays as a library API (the benches use it).
- `max_cells_per_tick` still caps cells per publish round.
- The README sections "The anti-entropy loop", "Coverage fanout", "Dirty rings and the peer frontier" and the fanout knob row still describe main. A pointer at the top of the Design notes says they do not apply here. They were not rewritten, to keep the diff small.

scuttlebutt.design_notes:
Implemented as specified: each round (shared scheduler unchanged) opens f=1 exchanges (defaults::GOSSIP_FANOUT=1, was 3) with distinct random peers. Flow is SYN digest -> peer replies with cells above the digest (oldest version first per origin, deepest backlog first) plus its own digest -> initiator sends the cells the peer lacks. No unsolicited cells; digests are sent every round even when nothing differs. AIMD is off. All of this is documented in crates/gabion/README.md "Design notes: Scuttlebutt", which also notes at the top that the later README sections still describe the baseline.

Adaptations (each is in the README with reasons):
1. Versions: a receiver keeps the origin's version for each cell. Main renumbered remote cells locally, which would make digests incomparable. Cells of an origin sit on a version-ordered intrusive list in CellStore, so answering a digest walks only the owed cells. Remote cells that arrive reordered insert by walking back from the tail.
2. UDP loss and reordering: the paper's "highest version received" digest needs a reliable ordered channel. Each cell carries a new 4-byte claim_gap column, certifying that no versions exist between version-gap and version. The receiver advances an origin's watermark only across claims that chain onto its current watermark, and never for a cell the store rejected. Cells above a hole are still merged (the join is idempotent) but the digest does not advance past the hole. Wire VERSION is bumped to 2, with new FLAG_DIGEST and FLAG_SYN and a new wire/digest.rs.
3. Digest size: a digest of N origins is 28 B each and does not fit one datagram at 80 or 300 origins. Digests are cut into frames that each name the node-id range [lo,hi] they cover. An origin in the range that the frame does not list is answered from version 0. Frames are therefore independently answerable and a lost frame costs only its range.
4. Reply budget: the paper's reply is one MTU. A reply here is bounded by max_cells_per_tick (4096, the same per-tick bound main uses) split into 1,400 B datagrams by the shared codec and limited by the send pool. One MTU per reply could not carry the offered load. Scuttle-depth is implemented as descending (newest held version minus digest version), the Cassandra ordering. I could not verify against the paper whether its "depth" ordering is descending or ascending by backlog.
5. Expired cells: merge_remote now takes now_millis and acknowledges, without storing, a cell whose bucket is already out of window for a known rule. Without this, a peer that had not yet expired a cell returned it right after the watermark reset, and quickcheck_sim_tick_expiration_removes_converged_cells failed.
6. Removed as main-only: dirty rings, peer frontier, repair lane, selection marks, fill_gossip_frame*, GOSSIP_COVERAGE_MARGIN, PeerEntry.node_id/peer_slot, AdminSnapshot.local_dirty_len/forwarded_dirty_len.
7. No-ops kept for the harness and adapters: CellStoreConfig.{local_dirty_capacity, forwarded_dirty_capacity, peer_capacity} are retained, documented as unused, and nothing reads them. last_effective_fanout, peak_effective_fanout and dirty_ticks now report exchanges opened per tick.
8. Server admin /snapshot JSON no longer has peers[].node_id or gossip.local_dirty_len/forwarded_dirty_len. In gabion-wasm the same snapshot fields are dropped and PeerView.node_id is set to None; the web TypeScript was not touched.
Known paper deviation: trailing version holes (the newest cell of an origin expiring while older ones live) are not certified. This costs a few resent cells until expiry and does not affect correctness.

owner-agg.design_notes:
Fixes for the audit:
MAJOR (owner broadcasts only changed origin cells): an owner now broadcasts the whole state of every key that changed, meaning every live cell it holds for that (rule,key) across all buckets and all contributors, which is Gubernator's key status. CellStore gained a per-key chain (key_heads: CellIndex keyed by hash(rule,key) to the head slot, plus key_next and key_prev columns, all sized at construction). Cells are linked on insert and unlinked in free_cell_at, and key_cells(rule, key_hash) iterates a key's cells. Nothing allocates after construction. At the broadcast tick the runtime pops queued changed cells and expands each one into its key's cells. A per-round mark in Outbox (broadcast_round) makes each key and each cell go out once per frame. Only cells whose owner is still Local are expanded. broadcast_batch_limit now counts keys, as in Gubernator, and the defaults, config, server and README docs say so. frame_handles is pre-sized to store capacity because a frame holds each live cell at most once.
Test restored: quickcheck_sim_partition_heals_without_overcount no longer has every contributor re-hit its keys after the heal. The restored form still failed for cold keys, because an owner's broadcast lost to the partition is not retried and a key that never changes again cannot be repaired. This is Gubernator's behaviour and the design is not given an anti-entropy repair. The test therefore makes one single node (node 0) hit each distinct key once after the heal and requires every node to reach the exact model. That one change is the repair condition, and it only works because broadcasts carry the whole key. The gabion-wasm tests partition_blocks_then_heal_converges and added_node_catches_up_by_gossip were weakened by the earlier spike to say only the changed cell arrives. They are restored to full convergence (8 and 51) and still need the key's next hit.
README "Design notes" is corrected: the key's whole state is broadcast, and the next change repairs any peer. It adds a "Batch limit" bullet and a "Queue overflow" bullet. The batch-limit bullet documents the deviation that Gubernator flushes as soon as 1,000 keys are queued and arms timers on the first queued item, while here the tickers free-run and the limit is a per-tick cap in keys. A sync is capped at max_cells_per_tick cells. Neither cap binds in any tested regime. The "Cells, not totals" bullet states the cost: prod-typical bytes/node/s rose from about 97 KB to about 270 KB, because a changed key is re-sent in full.
MINOR (sync-queue overflow drops the obligation): queue_sync and queue_all_local_cells now set requeue_local_cells when the queue is full. The sync tick first prunes settled entries, then sweeps every local cell that is not yet held by its owner (the sweep skips Route::Settled cells, otherwise a full queue of settled cells would starve the rest) and gathers the batch again. This is a new collect_sync_batch helper. The warning text is unchanged. The sweep costs O(store capacity) only while overflow persists or membership changed. A broadcast-queue overflow still drops the change, and the next change to the key repairs it (documented).
MINOR (send_queue_capacity silently clamped to 255): slot indexes are now u32 and only a minimum of 1 is enforced.
All earlier design notes still hold: UDP acks on sync and no acks or retries on broadcast, the FLAG_SYNC/FLAG_ACK header bits, the 100 ms cadences replacing main's rounds, the no-op harness fields, and the main-side threshold accounting is untouched.

minors.problem: A digest cannot tell a missing version from a superseded one. A node that holds an older version of a cell serves that stale cell to a requester that already holds a newer one. This spends the lagging node's repair budget on cells the receiver drops in the join. The README does not document it; it documents only the reverse direction.
minors.evidence: cells_lacked returns lacked = !entry.holds(seq). If B holds X@15 and A holds X@20, A's digest marks only 20 for that origin, so holds(15) is false and B sends X@15. A's MaxMerge ignores it (crdt.rs upsert: next == previous). Under loss the lagging side is exactly the one answering, so stale sends can crowd out cells A really lacks.

minors.problem: The note on the 256-sequence window covers late losses but not joiners. A node that has received any first-phase packet from origin O lists O with max M. Every live cell of O with sequence below M-256 is then taken as held and is never served to that joiner. The README's framing of 'about 2 sequences a second over a two-minute window' also does not give the real condition, which is per-origin rate × (rule window + bucket) ≤ 256.

bimodal.design_notes:
Audit issues fixed, all in commit 9f4cbf0.

**Major: repair budget.**
- The budget is now derived, not picked, and the arithmetic is documented in `gabion::defaults`.
- New constants: `GOSSIP_RECEIVE_BUFFER_BYTES` = 212,992 (Linux `rmem_default`), `GOSSIP_REPAIR_BUFFER_SHARE` = 2, `GOSSIP_REPAIR_CELL_WIRE_BYTES` = 82.
- The 82 bytes is the worst-case wire cost of one cell: 42 fixed per-cell columns, an 8-byte count, and two 16-byte dictionary entries in a packet that shares nothing.
- `GOSSIP_REPAIR_MAX_CELLS` = 212,992 / 2 / 82 = 1,298 cells (about 76 full packets), up from the arbitrary 512.
- The README design notes and the operator-knobs table state that loss and churn results are budget-bound at this value. They also say `repair_max_cells`, like `repair_period` (0.5, 1, 2 s), is a `GossipConfig` field meant to be swept.
- The 1,298 value was fixed before any loss run and not tuned afterwards.

**Minor: digest window.**
- The 256-sequence window is now `GOSSIP_DIGEST_WINDOW_WORDS` = 4 in `gabion::defaults`, with its rationale. `wire/digest.rs` derives `DIGEST_WORDS` and `DIGEST_WINDOW` from it.
- The README design notes name the regimes it cannot cover. Roughly, that is an origin stamping more than about 2 sequences per second over a two-minute window, such as long-window rules at high per-origin rates, or very high-rate regimes. In those, older losses are invisible to repair.
- Widening the window costs 8 bytes per word in every digest entry.

**Minor: repair ordering.**
- The README documents slot order as a deliberate non-adoption of the paper's most-recent-first optimization.
- Reason: recency across origins needs a sort or a second store scan per digest, and sequences compare only within one origin.
- The audit's rotation experiment showed ordering is not what drives the loss-20 result.

**Minor: peer removal during a broadcast.**
- Fixed in code: `handle_peer_event` now decrements `next` of every in-flight `Outgoing::All` when a peer at a lower index is removed, so no peer is skipped.
- A peer added mid-broadcast joins the tail of the walk, or misses that one packet; digest repair covers it. This is documented.
- No dedicated unit test, because `Outgoing` is private to `gossip::runtime`.

**Minor: stale README.**
- Removed the "Coverage fanout" section and the "Dirty rings and the peer frontier" section. Rewrote "How gossip works" intro, the anti-entropy loop diagram and text, the wire-frame notes (digest flags), the operator-knobs table, and the References and Contents entries.
- Added "The local change queue" section.
- Replaced "What we measured" with a pointer to the study harness, because those figures measured the replaced protocol. The figure SVGs are left in `figures/` untouched, since `bench/plot.py` in the untouchable harness crate writes them.
- Added a banner to `CRDT.md` saying its forwarded-ring, peer-frontier and repair-cursor sections describe the replaced protocol.
- The server and nginx adapter READMEs still document the now-inert fanout and forwarded and peer capacity knobs. This is noted in the design notes and not rewritten here.

**Unchanged from before.**
- The two-phase design, the wire format, the shared scheduler, and the no-op config fields (`fanout`, `forwarded_dirty_capacity`, `peer_capacity`, `GossipSettings::fanout`).
- `repair_period` and `repair_max_cells` are still not exposed as YAML or nginx keys.

az-hier.design_notes:
Documented in crates/gabion/README.md "Design notes".
Mechanism as spec: own cells to every in-zone peer plus one rendezvous-hash gateway per remote zone (weight = mix(origin node id, member addr); rank = (not suspect, weight, addr)); a gateway relays only cells that arrived in a non-relay packet from an origin outside its zone, only into its own zone, batched per local peer per relay round.
Adaptations, each minimal:
(1) Zone from address: zone = peer address truncated to zone_prefix_len=16 bits (PeerEvent/Peer untouched), standing in for EndpointSlice zone.
(2) UDP hop reliability: two cumulative-ack streams per peer pair. The own stream is sequenced by origin_sequence. The relay stream is sequenced by a per-node relay stamp kept in a per-cell-slot column, because main re-stamps merged cells per origin so no single global order exists for relayed cells. Each packet states the range (stream_lower, stream_upper] it closes, so a receiver advances its contiguous 'have' only when the range starts at or below it (gap-safe).
(3) Wire change: header 72 to 88 bytes, VERSION 2. min/max_origin_sequence (computed, unused) are replaced by ack_own, ack_relay, stream_lower, stream_upper; new FLAG_RELAY. Packets::with_stamps and Packets::abandon, and encode_header_only for standalone acks. Acks are therefore explicit on the wire and counted by the judge, not hidden in other fields (the prior spike patched cluster_id_hash and min_origin_sequence after encoding, which breaks HMAC).
(4) RTO = max(2*srtt, rto_floor=500 ms), srtt from one timed probe per stream, dropped on resend (Karn). On timeout the stream resumes from the last ack. A gateway whose own-stream ack misses the RTO is marked suspect and the next rank takes over, literal to spec with one miss. Hearing any packet from the suspect clears it. All-suspect falls back to plain rendezvous, so a zone always has a gateway. Failover is triggered only by missing acks.
(5) Standalone header-only acks go out only on heartbeat rounds, only to peers that sent cells and got no piggyback this round.
(6) Relay timing: a second Clock::ticker(relay_floor=5 ms) is polled only while relayed cells await forwarding, so relay rounds run at most every 5 ms and the first after a quiet spell is immediate. This is the design's own timing and the only change to scheduling; heartbeat and threshold rounds are main's, with Round::{Heartbeat,Threshold,Relay} replacing the single Tick outcome.
(7) Not implemented: aggregate=true Astrolabe aggregation (rule 1, no variant switches). The spec's 'one gateway per (origin, remote AZ)' is hard-wired.
(8) Parameters zone_prefix_len/rto_floor/relay_floor are GossipConfig fields with defaults GOSSIP_ZONE_PREFIX_LEN/GOSSIP_RTO_FLOOR_MS/GOSSIP_RELAY_FLOOR_MS in gabion::defaults. server, nginx and wasm configs set them from the defaults; no YAML knobs were added.
No-ops now: GossipConfig.fanout and rng_seed (the design is deterministic and has no random choice). The CRDT dirty rings and peer frontier are no longer used by the runtime. The runtime calls clear_dirty() after each mutation so the rings never fill or log 'dirty ring overflowed'. AdminSnapshot.local_dirty_len and forwarded_dirty_len therefore read 0. PeerEntry.peer_slot was removed.
Per-node state is bounded and sized at construction: scratch vectors and relay_stamp are sized to the cell capacity, and per-peer state is created on a discovery join and freed on a leave. A peer's stream state resets if its node id or incarnation changes. Packets from addresses not in discovery are merged but not acked (I-2).
